# Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅga (Vb 15)

**ID:** Vb 15
**Section:** Vibhaṅga (vb)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅga
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh02m.mul14.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅga* is the fifteenth chapter of the *Vibhaṅga*, the second treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Hazra 1994]. In the Pali Text Society edition, it occupies pages 293–305 [Jayatilleke 1963]. Like other major treatises of the *Vibhaṅga*, it provides systematic analysis through divisions such as the Sutta explanation (*suttantabhājaniya*) [Hazra 1994; Nyanatiloka 1938]. The treatise is structured around the four analytical discriminations (*catu-paṭisambhidā*, corresponding to Buddhist Sanskrit *pratisaṃvidā*): the discrimination of meaning (*attha-paṭisambhidā*), the discrimination of phenomena, causal conditions, or doctrine (*dhamma-paṭisambhidā*), the discrimination of language or verbal definition (*nirutti-paṭisambhidā*), and the discrimination of perspicuity or analytical insight (*paṭibhāna-paṭisambhidā*) [Jayatilleke 1963; Nyanatiloka 1938; Peoples 2013]. The text articulates these principles as systematic criteria for developing analytical knowledge, distinguishing between mundane and supramundane realizations [Peoples 2013].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Mentioned in: Arv 24 Catasraḥ Pratisaṁvidaḥ

**Sources**

- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pali Language and Literature (1994) — Confirmed the position of the text as the 15th chapter of the Vibhaṅga and its structural divisions.
- [Jayatilleke 1963] K.N. Jayatilleke, Early Buddhist Theory of Knowledge (1963) — Noted PTS pagination and described the four branches of logical analysis.
- [Nyanatiloka 1938] Nyanatiloka Mahāthera, Guide Through the Abhidhamma Piṭaka (1938) — Detailed the four discriminations and noted the Sutta-explanation section.
- [Peoples 2013] Dion Peoples, Buddhist Critical Thinking Skills (2013) — Discussed the four discriminations as analytical insights covering mundane and supramundane understandings.
